facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj was born at the Shivneri fort near Junnar in Pune district on 19 February 1630.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj was born at the Shivneri fort near Junnar in Pune district on the day of Phalgun Vadya Tritiya in the Shaka year 1551, that is on 19 February 1630.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj's birth date was Phalgun Vadya Tritiya in the Shaka year 1551.
facts.quote: on the day of Phalgun Vadya Tritiya in the Shaka year 1551

facts.text: Shahajiraje, the father of Shivaji Maharaj, was a pre-eminent Sardar in the Deccan.
facts.quote: Shahajiraje, the father of Shivaji Maharaj was a pre-eminent Sardar in the Deccan.

facts.text: The Mughals launched a campaign to conquer the Nizamshahi; the Adilshah of Bijapur allied with them.
facts.quote: The Mughals had launched a campaign to conquer the Nizamshahi Kingdom. The Adilshah of Bijapur allied with the Mughals in this campaign.

facts.text: Shahaji Maharaj tried to save the Nizamshahi by offering stiff resistance to the Mughals.
facts.quote: Shahaji Maharaj did not wish the Mughals to get an entry into the South. So he tried to save Nizamshahi by offering stiff resistance to the Mughals.

facts.text: The Nizamshahi was defeated and came to an end in 1636 CE.
facts.quote: The Nizamshahi was defeated and came to an end in 1636 CE.

facts.text: As a Sardar of the Adilshah, Shahajiraje held as jagir the Pune, Supe, Indapur and Chakan parganas between the Bheema and Neera rivers.
facts.quote: Shahajiraje became a Sardar of the Adilshah of Bijapur. The region comprising Pune, Supe, Indapur and Chakan parganas located between the Bheema and Neera rivers was vested in Shahajiraje as a jagir.

facts.text: The Adilshah also granted Shahajiraje the jagir of Bengaluru and neighbouring areas in Karnataka.
facts.quote: he also granted the jagir of Bengaluru and the neighbouring areas in Karnataka to Shahajiraje.

facts.text: Jahagir or jagir means the right to enjoy the revenue of a region; Sardars got this revenue instead of salaries.
facts.quote: Jahagir or jagir means the right to enjoy the revenue of a region. The Sardars in the service of rulers used to get the revenue of the region as income instead of getting salaries directly.

facts.text: Shahajiraje was an excellent archer and an expert with the sword, patta and spear; he won regions in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: He was an excellent archer. He was also an expert in using the sword, patta and spear. ... He had won many regions in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

facts.text: Shahajiraje arranged excellent education for Shivaji at Bengaluru and is known as the Swaraj visionary.
facts.quote: While Shivaji and Jijabai were at Bengaluru, he had arranged for providing excellent education to Shivaji ... That is why, he is known as Swaraj visionary.

facts.text: Shahajiraje sent Shivaji and Jijabai from Bengaluru to Pune with loyal and competent associates.
facts.quote: He sent Shivaji and Jijabai from Bengaluru to Pune with loyal and competent associates.

facts.text: Jijabai was the daughter of Sardar Lakhujiraje Jadhav of Sindkhedraja in Buldhana district.
facts.quote: Jijabai was the daughter of the great Sardar Lakhujiraje Jadhav of Sindkhedraja in Buldhana district.

facts.text: At a young age, Jijabai received military training and education in various subjects.
facts.quote: At a young age, she had received military training as well as education in various subjects.

facts.text: At times, Veermata Jijabai gave verdicts to resolve the problems of the people.
facts.quote: At times, she undertook the task of giving verdicts for resolving the problems of people.

facts.text: Jijabai instilled in Shivaji modesty, truthfulness, oratory, vigilance, courage and fearlessness.
facts.quote: She instilled in him values like modesty, truthfulness, oratory, vigilance, courage and fearlessness.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj started founding the Swaraj in the Maval region, full of hills and valleys and not easily accessible.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj started the work of founding the Swaraj in the Maval region. The Maval terrain is full of hills and valleys and is not easily accessible.

facts.text: Associates of Shivaji Maharaj included Yesaji Kank, Baji Pasalkar, Bapuji Mudgal, the Narhekar Deshpande brothers, Kavji Kondhalkar, Jiva Mahala, Tanaji Malusare, Kanhoji Jedhe, Bajiprabhu Deshpande and Dadaji Narasprabhu Deshpande.
facts.quote: Among them were Yesaji Kank, Baji Pasalkar, Bapuji Mudgal, Narhekar Deshpande brothers, Kavji Kondhalkar, Jiva Mahala, Tanaji Malusare, Kanhoji Jedhe, Bajiprabhu Deshpande and Dadaji Narasprabhu Deshpande.

facts.text: The Maval valley in the Sahyadris was in the Pune jagir of Shivaji Maharaj and is also known as 'Bara Maval'.
facts.quote: Maval valley in the Sahyadris was a region in the Pune jagir of Shivaji Maharaj. It is also known as 'Bara Maval'.

facts.text: Bara Maval has twelve parts, including Pavan Maval, Hirdas Maval, Gunjan Maval, Andar Maval, Nane Maval and Korbarse Maval.
facts.quote: Bara Maval : (1) Pavan Maval (2) Hirdas Maval (3) Gunjan Maval ... (10) Andar Maval (11) Nane Maval (12) Korbarse Maval

facts.text: The royal seal (Rajmudra) carries Sanskrit lines: the seal of Shivaji, son of Shahaji, will grow in splendour like the new moon and denotes the welfare of the people.
facts.quote: 'This seal will grow in splendour like the new moon. This seal of Shivaji, the son of Shahaji, receiving homage from the whole world denotes the welfare of the people.'

facts.text: The Rajmudra inscription expresses gratitude to his father, confidence that Swaraj would expand, and commitment to the welfare of his subjects.
facts.quote: Through this inscription, Maharaj has expressed his gratitude towards his father, his confidence that Swaraj would expand continuously, ... his commitment to the welfare of his subjects

facts.text: The forts within Shivaji Maharaj's jagir were under Adilshah's control; if one had forts, one ruled the land.
facts.quote: The forts situated within the jagir of Shivaji Maharaj were not under his control, but were under the control of Adilshah. ... If one had forts, one ruled the land.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj captured the forts of Torana, Murumbdev, Kondhana and Purandar and laid the foundation of Swaraj.
facts.quote: He captured the forts of Torana, Murumbdev, Kondhana and Purandar, and laid the foundation of Swaraj.

facts.text: He repaired Murumbdev and renamed it Rajgad; Rajgad was the first capital of the Swaraj.
facts.quote: He repaired the fort Murumbdev and renamed it Rajgad. Rajgad was the first capital of the Swaraj.

facts.text: The Mores of Javali, the Ghorpades of Mudhol and the Sawants of Sawantwadi were Adilshahi Sardars opposed to Swaraj.
facts.quote: There were the Mores of Javali, the Ghorpades of Mudhol, the Sawants of Sawantwadi, and other Sardars in the Adilshahi. They were opposed to the cause of the founding of Swaraj.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj attacked Javali, the region of Chandrarao More in Satara district, and captured it in 1656 CE.
facts.quote: Chandrarao More of Javali in Satara district was a powerful Sardar in the Adilshahi. ... Shivaji Maharaj attacked Javali and captured that region in 1656 CE.

facts.text: After Javali he captured Raigad, gained huge wealth, and built the Pratapgad fort in the Javali valley.
facts.quote: Then he also captured Raigad. He attained a huge amount of wealth from Javali. ... He built the Pratapgad fort in the Javali valley.

facts.text: He captured Kalyan and Bhiwandi, met the Siddi, Portuguese and British powers, and concentrated on building a navy.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj captured Kalyan and Bhiwandi on the Konkan Coast. There he came into contact with the Siddi, Portuguese and British powers ... Therefore, he concentrated on building a navy.

facts.text: Badi Sahiba, looking after the Adilshahi administration, sent Afzalkhan to curb Shivaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: At that time, the Badi Sahiba was looking after the administration of the Adilshahi. She sent Afzalkhan, a powerful and experienced Adilshahi General, to curb Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: Afzalkhan came from Bijapur to Wai; he knew the Wai region well.
facts.quote: Afzalkhan came from Bijapur to Wai. He knew the Wai region well.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj met Afzalkhan on 10 November 1659 at the foot of Pratapgad near Wai; Afzalkhan attempted treachery and was killed.
facts.quote: A meeting of Shivaji Maharaj and Afzalkhan took place on 10 November 1659 at the foot of Pratapgad near Wai. At the meeting, Afzalkhan attempted treachery. In retaliation, Shivaji Maharaj killed Afzalkhan.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj paid compensation to wounded soldiers, rewarded brave fighters and treated captured enemy soldiers well.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj paid compensation to the soldiers who were wounded in the battle. He rewarded those who had fought well. Those soldiers and officers of Afzalkhan's army who fell into the hands of Shivaji Maharaj's army were given a good treatment.

facts.text: After Afzalkhan, Shivaji Maharaj captured Panhala, Vasantgad and Khelna, and renamed Khelna 'Vishalgad'.
facts.quote: Shivaji Maharaj captured the Adilshahi forts of Panhala, Vasantgad and Khelna. He renamed Khelna as 'Vishalgad'.

facts.text: In 1660 CE the Adilshah sent Siddi Jauhar, Sardar of the Karnul region, against Shivaji Maharaj and gave him the title 'Salabatkhan'.
facts.quote: the Adilshah sent Siddi Jauhar, the Sardar of the Karnul region, against Shivaji Maharaj in 1660 CE. The Adilshah gave Siddi the title 'Salabatkhan'.

facts.text: Rustum-e-Jaman, Baji Ghorpade and Afzalkhan's son Fazalkhan helped Siddi Jauhar.
facts.quote: Rustum-e-Jaman, Baji Ghorpade and Afzalkhan's son Fazalkhan were also there to help Siddi Jauhar.

facts.text: Siddi's soldiers besieged Panhala for about five months; Netoji Palkar's attempt to raise the siege failed as his forces were meagre.
facts.quote: Siddi's soldiers laid siege to the fort for about five months. ... Netoji Palkar tried to raise the siege by attacking Siddi's army from outside, but he couldn't succeed in it as his forces were meagre.

facts.text: Shiva Kashid, who resembled Shivaji Maharaj, left in a palanquin by the 'Raj-dindi' gate and sacrificed himself for Swaraj.
facts.quote: Shiva Kashid, a brave youth came forward. He resembled Shivaji Maharaj in looks. He dressed up like Shivaji Maharaj and sat in a palanquin. The palanquin left by the 'Raj-dindi' gate. ... Shiva Kashid sacrificed himself on this occasion for Swaraj.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj left Panhala by another difficult route with Baji Prabhu Deshpande, Bandal Deshmukh and chosen soldiers.
facts.quote: He was accompanied by Baji Prabhu Deshpande, Bandal Deshmukh and some chosen soldiers.

facts.text: Bajiprabhu Deshpande checked Siddi's army at the Ghod pass near Gajapur and died a hero's death.
facts.quote: Bajiprabhu Deshpande checked Siddi's army at the Ghod pass near Gajapur. He fought with the greatest valour. Bajiprabhu died a hero's death in this battle.

facts.text: On the way to Vishalgad, he crushed the Adilshahi Sardars Dalvi of Palwan and Surve of Shringarpur.
facts.quote: While going to Vishalgad, Maharaj also crushed the opposition of the Adilshahi Sardars Dalvi of Palwan and Surve of Shringarpur.

facts.text: Aurangzeb sent the Mughal Sardar Shaistakhan to the Deccan; he invaded the Pune province.
facts.quote: Aurangzeb, who had ascended the throne of Delhi, had sent Shaistakhan, a Mughal Sardar to the Deccan. He had invaded the Pune province.

facts.text: Not wishing to fight two enemies at once, Shivaji Maharaj made a treaty with the Adilshah and returned Panhala.
facts.quote: Maharaj realised that it would not be prudent to fight two enemies at one and the same time. Therefore, after reaching Vishalgad safely, he entered into a treaty with the Adilshah. As per the treaty, he returned the fort of Panhala to the Adilshah.
